methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Olympian Motors is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Eren Canarslan and Jasmine Sungu that has raised $9.6M to date. The transportation sector includes six private peers of varying stage and maturity (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, EarthGrid), though no public comparables exist. A narrow peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum sample thresholds.

The stage-progression method was the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using the $9.6M raised as a valuation proxy, a 2.5x step-up multiplier—typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement in the sector—implies a valuation of $24M. This method directly reflects the capital deployed and expected equity value creation at the next funding milestone.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $20M to $28M, with a median of $24M. The compressed range reflects reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable seed-stage exits or recent fundings in transportation hardware, limiting external benchmarking. The valuation is sensitive to assumptions around time-to-Series A, capital efficiency relative to peer norms, and product validation milestones. Tightening this range would require either achieving measurable product or market milestones or acquiring additional seed-stage transportation comparables with disclosed terms.
